name: Hair removal glove (Silk n Soft)

card.summary: A rough-textured mitt rubbed on the skin to rub off fine hair by friction, giving a smoother, hair-free look on arms and legs.
card.aka: hair eraser mitt, friction hair removal glove
card.note: Rubbing too hard can irritate skin; the thin skin around the eyes is not suited to friction.

quick.overview:
A hair removal glove is an abrasive mitt that is rubbed in circular motions over the skin so that friction wears down fine hair, leaving the area looking smooth. Versions sold under names such as Silk n Soft are marketed as a tool-free way to smooth arms and legs.

General descriptions of friction hair removal say it suits fine hair on the lower legs and arms. Users describe the result as short-lived, and independent trials of specific products are limited.
quick.how: Directions for mitts of this kind generally call for light circular rubbing over dry or lightly wet skin, repeated as hair regrows. Users also use similar exfoliating gloves in the shower to smooth skin before or after shaving.
quick.risks: Rubbing too hard can irritate the skin, and the area around the eyes has thin skin that cannot tolerate friction. People with sensitive or acne-prone skin may find friction irritating.

lead: A hair removal glove, also called a hair eraser mitt, is an abrasive pad worn on the hand and rubbed over the skin to remove fine hair through friction. The version in this entry is sold under the Silk n Soft name. It appeals to people who want smooth arms and legs without shaving, waxing or creams.

Friction hair removal as a category is generally described as best for fine hair on the lower legs and arms, with a motion alternating clockwise and counter-clockwise, and with cautions against rubbing hard.

Forum users in the strength and fitness community mention exfoliating gloves as a way to smooth the skin, for example a T Nation reply on hair removal and acne suggests that the exfoliation from shaving may have helped and recommends a poof or exfoliating glove with a moisturising body wash.[1]

chain: Fine hair wears away at the surface
Smoother, hair-free-looking skin for a short period
angle.text: The mitt temporarily removes or breaks off fine hair so the skin looks smooth, for example before a physique photo or beach season. Results last until the hair grows back.

infobox: Lower legs and arms with fine hair

paras: The glove has an abrasive surface, and its action is mechanical: rubbing removes hair at or near the skin surface. It is related to other friction methods such as emery cloth. Product pages and retailer listings describe it alongside shaving, waxing, tweezing and depilatories as one of the options for removing body hair.
Gym and physique communities discuss body-hair removal for presentation, and exfoliating gloves come up in the context of smooth skin and acne-prone skin.[1] Individual accounts are anecdotal.

Exfoliating and friction products can irritate skin if used with too much pressure, and are not meant for the thin skin around the eyes. People with skin conditions often take advice from a dermatologist.
